# Measured memory system - nrf52840

*🤖WARNING🤖: This file LLM generated and may read oddly. Will eventually be human-edited for that real-life touch and typos.*

`memmap/1 nrf52840 cortex-m4 64000000 systick 64000000 counters,icache,ramfunc`

| property | measured | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| read width | 16 bytes | high |
| fill unit | unknown | none |
| latch | 1 entry x 16 B, depth 1; differential 3 cyc at icache=0 cacheprof=0; no knob reaches it | high |
| cache | none (no multi-line data reuse in any configuration) | high |
| replacement policy | unknown | none |
| waitstate scaling | unknown | none |
| twin calibration | unknown | none |

| knob | read width | latch | data reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icache` | no effect | no effect | no effect |
| `cacheprof` | no effect | no effect | no effect |

fill_unit caveats:
- Every knob setting saturates at the same stride, so no separate fill unit is distinguishable from the read width.

cache caveats:
- No data-side cache: in every knob setting the target is lost after the latch's own depth. Reuse that is not back-to-back is not retained anywhere.

replacement_policy caveats:
- LRU and FIFO are NOT separable with `memmap/1`'s two-argument primitives, and that is a property of the primitives rather than of the part. `walk` and `evict` produce a monotone reference string and `chase` a cyclic one, and on a cyclic string over capacity+1 lines LRU and FIFO evict exactly the same line at every step. Separating them needs a reference string that re-touches an already-resident line before bringing in a new one - which is what the optional third `evict` argument provides, and what a shim that does not implement it leaves unreachable.
- No multi-line cache was found, so there is no replacement policy to infer: a 1-entry latch has no victim to choose.

waitstate_scaling caveats:
- This part exposes no wait-state knob.

twin_calibration caveats:
- This part exposes no wait-state knob, so there is no setting at which a flash access is known to be free and the twin cannot be calibrated this way.

Cross-checks:
- Cross-check: the latch granularity equals the flash read width (16 B), as it does on every part in this repository.
- GAP: this part advertises `counters` - hardware hit/miss registers that `PROTOCOL.md` calls an independent instrument - and the capture contains no counter reading. Every claim here rests on timing alone, with a cross-check available and unused.
